acceptance: A re-review round (round 2 or later) of the same change reviews the delta since the last reviewed tree plus the open findings of the earlier rounds, not the whole diff afresh.
A finding on a line that an earlier round reviewed and did not flag is reported as a late finding: it is filed as an item and does not block, unless it is CRITICAL.
A test drives three rounds over a fixture change and asserts the round-3 input is the delta and that a late HIGH does not block.
fix: Give the review seats a round-aware input: the delta since the last reviewed tree and the prior findings. Classify late findings on already-reviewed lines as items, not blockers, so the convergence rule (no round 4) can converge.
source: console builds of 2026-11-23: #1690, #1691, the YAML floor check and C13
summary: On 2026-11-23 a fresh architecture seat run on the whole diff at each round found new HIGH findings in code that earlier rounds had passed, on four changes (#1690 r4: 4 HIGH, #1691, the YAML check r3: 3 HIGH after an r2 PASS, rank-5 design r3 reversing an r2 instruction). Each round re-reads the whole diff, so the finding set does not shrink and the no-round-4 rule forces an escalation or an ad hoc delta review every time.
title: Re-review rounds review the delta and the open findings, so reviews converge
